slides.title: Course algorithms in Rust
slides.main: The same ideas, but with slices, generics and standard collections; unsigned numbers need care.

slides.title: Counting operations
slides.main: The number of comparisons does not depend on the machine: easy to check in tests.

slides.title: Binary search
slides.main: The middle lo + (hi − lo) / 2 does not overflow; the comparison is the Ordering enum.

slides.title: Insertion sort
slides.main: swap exchanges neighbors without copying values: works for strings too.

slides.title: Merge sort
slides.main: split_at divides a slice without copies; the merge is stable: equal elements keep their order.

slides.title: Heap and top-k
slides.main: BinaryHeap is a max-heap; Reverse turns it into a min-heap.

slides.title: Hash tables in algorithms
slides.main: Sorted letters are the group key; entry().or_default() inserts and updates in one lookup.

slides.title: Graph and breadth-first search
slides.main: Vertices are indices; Option<u32> in the distance array encodes "unreachable".

slides.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
slides.main: Stale heap entries are skipped on extraction; infinity is u64::MAX.

slides.title: Dynamic programming
slides.main: Two table rows are enough: memory drops from the product of lengths to one length.

slides.title: Disjoint set union
slides.main: Path compression and union by size: almost constant time.

slides.title: Integer traps
slides.main: usize is unsigned: 3 − 5 is not −2. Pick an explicit operation.

slides.title: Chapter summary
slides.main: Algorithms in Rust: slices, generics, standard collections and careful arithmetic.
